commands.command: Architecture issue A investigation: coverage:complete semantics
commands.summary: CONFIRMED REAL: governance/verification.json's 'release' profile declared coverage:complete with zero platform-specific step declarations. _coverage()'s satisfied formula for complete mode reduced to 'not required_unavailable' with no reference to any cross-platform requirement, so a single Windows host could report coverage.mode=complete, coverage.satisfied=true on a profile that never represented Linux/macOS/Android/iOS at all. Reproduced with a focused failing-then-passing test pair before any fix (test_complete_coverage_without_required_platforms_declaration_is_rejected, test_complete_coverage_with_multi_platform_requirement_never_fabricates_pass_on_one_host).

Added an optional profile-level required_platforms declaration to the schema (repopact/schemas/verification-profile.schema.json) and to both the Python semantic validator (repopact/verification.py _validate_semantics) and the shared Rust validator (repopact-validation/src/verification.rs validate_semantics): a profile declaring coverage:complete without a non-empty required_platforms now fails validation outright (new diagnostic verification.complete-coverage-missing-required-platforms). _coverage() now computes satisfied for complete mode as 'this run's platform covers the entire required_platforms set'; any other required platform is reported in a new missing_platforms field rather than silently assumed to have run. governance/verification.json's release profile now declares required_platforms: [windows, linux, macos] (Android/iOS excluded per this pass's own guidance -- they are not part of RepoPact's PyPI wheel matrix).

commands.command: Architecture issue B investigation: governed release surface
commands.summary: Inspected pyproject.toml (maturin bin-backend building repopact-engine + repopact as platform-specific wheels), README.md's only public install instruction (pip install repopact), release_build.py's explicit assertion that a wheel 'must be platform-specific because it contains native binaries', and Decision 0043 item 11 ('cross-platform local execution is part of the contract'). Conclusion: the Python wheel/sdist pair is RepoPact's current governed, published release surface; the Tauri Workbench native packages proven installable in WI060/WI062 are explicitly local-operator-install artifacts, not part of the public PyPI release contract (WI062 itself scoped signing/public distribution as separate work). Outcome 1 applies: release_local's wheel/sdist-centered scope is honest and correct as-is; required_platforms=[windows, linux, macos] on the release profile correctly represents the real multi-platform wheel matrix without fabricating android/ios requirements.

commands.command: repopact.cli inspection for 'verify' and grouped 'release' subcommands
commands.summary: CONFIRMED REAL GAP: repopact/cli.py had NO 'verify' subcommand and NO grouped 'release' subcommand at all, despite README.md and docs/guides/local-ci-cd.md documenting `repopact verify quick|ci|release` and `repopact release verify|build|inspect|publish` as the canonical operator-facing workflow. Only the pre-WI046 hyphenated `release-build` compatibility command existed. verify_cli.py and release_local.py each have working standalone `main()` entry points reachable via `python -m repopact.verify_cli` / `python -m repopact.release_local` (which is what both hosted workflow adapters correctly use), but the documented unified `repopact` console command silently lacked the wiring.

commands.command: repopact.cli fix: wire verify and release subcommands
commands.summary: Added `verify` and `release` subparsers using argparse.REMAINDER that delegate the remaining argv verbatim to verify_cli.main() / release_local.main(), so no second argument-parsing definition is maintained and no semantics are duplicated. Verified `repopact verify quick --root .` and `repopact release verify --root .` now work end-to-end through the installed console-script surface, matching the documentation exactly.
